incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: streaming-decode p99 spike observed in us-west-2 cluster (fleet: inference-prod-ww). Alert threshold crossed at 2026-03-15T09:14:49Z.

alice (runtime): noticed after the 03:00 UTC rollout of trt8-driver-535.21 + compilepath v2.3.1 with the new "optimize-tiling" flag. p95 is bumped but p99/tail is what looks catastrophic — streaming stalls and context-page wait timeouts.

ben (oncall): ack. thanks for the flag. marking high-priority, paging SRE. who's got a quick mitigation? any customer-facing impact?

carmen (sre): digging into grafana now. initial numbers: baseline p95 ~110ms -> 280ms, p99 ~420ms -> 2.1s on streaming endpoints. error rate small but request queueing increased (inflight > capacity). See panels: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streaming/inference-p95-p99?orgId=1 :eyes:

alice (runtime): reproducer on a canary node shows decode kernel hitting frequent GPU pagefaults and long NVLINK stalls. logs nearby:

```
2026-03-15T09:12:05Z runtime[decode]: kernel: compilepath_v2.3.1: loaded kernel trt8_flashattn_v2.4
2026-03-15T09:12:05Z runtime[decode]: ERROR pagefault: ctx=0x7f9b1234 wait_ms=1820 stack=decode_exec+0x1f4
2026-03-15T09:12:06Z runtime[decode]: stall_detected: prefix_kv_cache_miss -> full-eviction
```

alice (runtime): the pattern looks like a change in the kernel/driver interaction with FlashAttention memory tiling that increases short-lived pagewalks under streaming workloads. batch workloads aren't as impacted.

eric (infra): driver 535.21 was pushed as part of infra kernel-driver bump this morning. can we roll the driver on canary back to 532.x?

ben (oncall): please do canary rollback immediately. also start mitigations we can do without infra patch: reduce max_frame_tokens, enable aggressive prefix caching (per-route), and fallback to quantized model variant for affected models.

carmen (sre): executing mitigation checklist:
- pinned routing for high-traffic routes to older model-variant (q4_0)
- enabled prefix_kv_cache=true for streaming routes
- adjusted autoscale throttle (scale-in cooloff -> 30s) to avoid flapping

alice (runtime): commands I ran on the canary pool:
```
# pin to older runtime image
kubectl -n inference set image ds/runtime runtime=image:runtime-2026-03-14-532driver
# toggle compile flag off
kubectl -n inference set env ds/runtime OPTIMIZE_TILING=false
```

alice (runtime): after those changes p99 on canary dropped from ~2.1s -> ~350ms within 90s. on prod the global p99 is still up but trending down where route pins applied.

ben (oncall): good short-term. customer impact? any escalations open?

carmen (sre): we have two customer support tickets flagged severity-2: slow responses for streaming transcripts (timeouts between 3-6s). estimated affected requests ~2.3% of total streaming traffic, error budget burn ~4% of daily SLO. advised support to notify customers about transient degradation while we mitigate.

alice (runtime): triage findings:
- root cause hypothesis: compilepath v2.3.1 + trt8-driver-535.21 changes to memory layout + FlashAttention v2.4 kernel causing increased transient GPU pagefaults under streaming (small batch, long context) workloads.
- repro: enable optimize-tiling + trt8-driver-535.21 + flashattn v2.4 on short-stream workload.

alice (runtime): short-term mitigations attempted:
- rollback driver on canary (work)
- disable optimize-tiling flag (work)
- fall back model variant -> q4_0 (work but lowers perf slightly)
- enable prefix_kv_cache aggressive TTL (work)

ben (oncall): next steps for on-call handoff -> we need a durable mitigation and plan to rollback or hotpatch. please prepare a runbook for the day shift.

alice (runtime): preparing the runbook now. key options:
1) infra rollback to driver 532.x across prod (requires infra change window)
2) runtime hotpatch to disable optimize-tiling by default and ship a config rollout (fast, controlled)
3) hotpatch FlashAttention kernel revert (requires rebuild + rollout)
4) progressive canary of each option with telemetry bake (p99, pagefaults, stall_count)

carmen (sre): telemetry we need for confirmation:
- per-node GPU pagefault count (nvml)
- decode stall_count and stall_duration (runtime metrics)
- route-level p95/p99 for 1h rolling windows

alice (runtime): I've added a dedicated dashboard and a csv export of affected traces. link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/incident/kernel-tiling-2026-03-15

eric (infra): started driver rollback on one prod AZ as low blast radius test. I pushed image: runtime-2026-03-14-532driver to nodepool-prod-az1. will monitor.

ben (oncall): good. assign to daytime owners: david (eng) for runtime patch, eric for driver rollback coordination, carmen for SRE monitoring and customer comms. I'll hand off at 09:20Z.

ben (oncall): @david you're up for owning the next shift. priority: fully document repro, finalize durable mitigation path, coordinate rollback timeline with infra and CS communications. :thumbsup:

alice (runtime): notes for handoff to @david:
- repro script: https://ci.redwood.example/job/repro/1234 (parameterize driver+flashattn+flag)
- recent canary logs: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/5213456789/canary-logs.tar.gz
- commands used to mitigation (see above)

david (eng): taking over. I'll validate the runtime hotpatch option first (disable optimize-tiling via feature flag). plan: create a canary rollout to 5% of streaming nodes, wait 10m, check p99 and pagefaults, then ramp. If not healthy, coordinate full infra driver rollback.

carmen (sre): CS notified: templated update sent to affected customers, tag #incident-5213456789. support has applied temporary routing workarounds for customer-specific routes.

ben (oncall): ending on-call handoff: summary posted to incidents channel and pager notes. escalation level: Sev2, mitigation in place, owners assigned. please update this thread with any changes. :white_check_mark:

incidents-bot: Incident 5213456789 status changed -> mitigated (partial) at 2026-03-15T09:22:03Z by alice (runtime). Full resolution pending follow-ups and infra rollback decision.

david (eng): logging next actions in tracker: https://tracker.redwood.example/ISSUE-1127 (runtime-hotpatch vs driver-rollback)

alice (runtime): added a checklist item to run the post-mortem eval-suite covering streaming prompt sets to ensure no quality regressions if we revert to older kernels.

carmen (sre): I'll keep watch on p99 and reopen paging if we see >=10% regression vs current baseline. tagging this thread for follow-up 24h after final rollout.

ben (oncall): thanks everyone. nice quick work on mitigations. will check back at 09:45Z for status update. :coffee:
